name: Trumpism
summary: Trumpism is the American right-wing populist movement built around Donald Trump and the 'Make America Great Again' slogan. It combines economic nationalism (tariffs, Buy American), immigration restriction, an America First foreign policy, social conservatism and hostility to the 'establishment', media and universities, with a strong, personalised executive. Scholars debate whether it is a coherent ideology or a style, and some describe illiberal or authoritarian tendencies.
scope: The mainstream movement as expressed in Trump's 2017 and 2025 inaugural addresses, the 2024 Republican platform and scholarly descriptions of the movement's components (right-wing populism, national conservatism, economic nationalism, Christian nationalism). Both Trump administrations are covered, with the second administration's foreign-policy record used for foreign-policy answers. Pre-2015 Republican orthodoxy, libertarian and neoconservative strands are not followed. Many economic and philosophical answers are low-confidence because the movement is thin and leader-centred.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The platform stresses price transparency, choice and competition rather than state-guaranteed coverage.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wages are not addressed in the platform, and working-class appeals coexist with business-friendly conservatism. Inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Deregulation and energy production sit beside tariffs and Buy American rules, so adherents do not simply trust markets over government. Inferred.

public-ownership.rationale: The platform backs private energy and industry production and has no public-ownership plank.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The platform seeks to make the Trump tax cuts permanent and add further cuts.

unions-good.rationale: Appeals to industrial workers coexist with a Republican business coalition; no settled position. Inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: The platform lists property and constitutional freedoms among rights to defend, though without absolutist language.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Deregulation and permitting reform are central, although hostility to some firms (tech, outsourcers) is also present.

cut-welfare.rationale: The platform promises no cuts to Social Security and Medicare, yet opposes benefits for illegal immigrants and favours work requirements; adherents are split.

worker-ownership.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the platform's private-enterprise orientation.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Security and law-and-order themes are strong, but free-speech and anti-'weaponization' themes cut against surveillance. Inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The platform proposes a fentanyl blockade, action against cartels and locking up violent offenders.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The inaugural address pledges to end government censorship and restore free speech; the platform bars federal collusion in censorship.

strong-leader.rationale: Scholars describe a maximal unitary executive and personalist leadership, with Trump saying Article II lets him 'do whatever I want'.

state-harmful.rationale: Trumpism seeks to shrink and redirect the state (DOGE) but relies on it heavily for borders, tariffs and policing.

limit-guns.rationale: The platform defends the right to keep and bear arms as a core constitutional freedom.

empower-police-military.rationale: The platform promises to rebuild police departments, protect officers and build the most powerful military in the world.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the platform's social conservatism.

decide-locally.rationale: Abortion and education are returned to the states, yet the executive overrides sanctuary jurisdictions and federalises policing in DC.

rehabilitation.rationale: The platform emphasises punishing offenders ('lock up violent offenders') and backing police.

traditional-family.rationale: The platform promotes the sanctity of marriage and support for working parents.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The platform is silent and Trump has accepted it, while social-conservative and evangelical factions oppose it.

abortion-legal.rationale: The platform leaves abortion to states and a vote, opposes late-term abortion and supports birth control and IVF; the base leans pro-life.

more-religion-public.rationale: The platform sets up a task force against anti-Christian bias and backs prayer in schools; Christian nationalists are a major faction.

separate-church-state.rationale: Christian nationalism is a documented faction, and the platform stresses religious expression in public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The inaugural address ends attempts to 'socially engineer race and gender' in favour of a colorblind, merit-based society.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Official policy is stated as 'there are only two genders: male and female'.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Patriotism, national tradition and America First are central, and scholars list neo-nationalism among its components.

gradual-change.rationale: Trumpism is disruptive of established institutions and norms rather than gradualist.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The inaugural address halts illegal entry, and the platform pledges mass deportation, an end to chain migration and a wall.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The administration withdrew from or defunded international bodies and opposed international cooperation.

free-trade.rationale: The 2017 inaugural address says protection will lead to great prosperity and strength; the platform backs baseline tariffs.

nation-first.rationale: 'From this day forward, it's going to be only America First.'

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The 2025 strategy largely drops democracy and rights promotion, and the platform urges avoiding unnecessary interventions.

open-borders.rationale: Halting all illegal entry and completing the border wall are core pledges.

limit-growth.rationale: The inaugural address declares an energy emergency and 'drill, baby, drill'; the platform ends the Green New Deal.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The address ends the Green New Deal and EV mandate and treats the energy emergency as one of supply; climate change is not discussed.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No stated doctrine on technology; inferred as neutral.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The platform seeks energy 'from all sources, including nuclear'.

revolution-justified.rationale: The platform stresses law and order and elections; the January 6 episode is contested. Inferred.

experts-over-public.rationale: Scholars identify anti-intellectualism and anti-establishment populism as components.

central-planning.rationale: The platform is pro-market and anti-'Marxist'; Trump rhetoric is hostile to socialism. Inferred from this.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from private-enterprise orientation.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; the platform's tax plank is lower taxes and tariffs.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The platform seeks tax cuts but does not name inheritance taxes; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; the platform stresses work and opposes new benefits for illegal immigrants. Inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The platform supports baseline tariffs and Buy American rules, and the 2025 address pledges to 'tariff and tax foreign countries'.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The platform backs Buy American and Hire American rules, defence-industrial revival and contract bans on outsourcers.

widespread-small-property.rationale: No stated position; populist rhetoric favours ordinary owners but policy is business-friendly.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wholly outside the platform and pro-market; inferred from its opposition to Marxism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The platform opposes a central bank digital currency and backs the dollar's reserve role but does not seek to abolish the Fed.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; the platform has no such planks.

one-party-rule.rationale: The platform operates within multiparty elections and demands voter ID and citizenship proof; scholars note illiberal tendencies.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; American republican patriotism makes monarchy alien. Inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: Adherents claim to defend the people's will, but scholars document illiberal tendencies and disputes over election results.

direct-votes.rationale: The platform invokes 'a vote of the People' on abortion but has no general direct-democracy plank.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from strong national unity and sovereignty themes.

natural-rulers.rationale: Anti-elite rhetoric coexists with leader-centred personalism; inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: Official statements condemn violence while the January 6 episode and pardons divide adherents.

war-builds-character.rationale: Success is measured by 'the wars we never get into' and Trump casts himself as peacemaker.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The platform seeks religious liberty rather than scripture-based law, though Christian nationalists in the movement go further.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The platform wants more police and military authority, not privatised ones; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: The address pledges 'the strongest military the world has ever seen'; the platform seeks the most powerful force in the world.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Official rhetoric is civic ('one people, one nation under God', colorblind), though scholars describe nativist and white-identity strands.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Populism frames politics as people versus establishment and stresses national unity, not class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The address calls for a colorblind, merit-based society.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from state-centred sovereignty and energy development priorities.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from America First and opposition to race-conscious policy.

civilizational-union.rationale: The 2025 strategy talks of civilizational concerns but pursues unilateral national interests; no political unions.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Transactional framing of foreign policy and business-minded style; inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The platform emphasises individual constitutional rights such as guns, speech and religion; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Resource development and drilling are prioritised; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Trumpism calls for industrial revival and restored manufacturing.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Support for crypto and defence tech sits beside no stated enthusiasm for disruption of institutions. Inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; split between libertarian and religious conservative strands.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from personalist, anti-technocratic style.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The platform defends free speech online and opposes a CBDC but is silent on encryption.

restore-past-order.rationale: The 'Make America Great Again' slogan and the 'golden age' promise are restorationist.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Commentators note a lack of coherent philosophy and a pragmatic, deal-oriented style.

direct-action.rationale: The platform works through elections and executive action; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: No stated position in the sources; adherents are pragmatic about means, so neutral is inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Opposed to the point of irrelevance given its industrial-revival message.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Alien to a pro-market platform; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The address stresses merit, not need-based distribution.

production-for-use.rationale: A pro-market platform accepts profit-driven production; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Pro-business platform with no exploitation theory; inferred.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The platform opposes Marxism explicitly ('Marxist prosecutors').

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The platform is pro-capitalist and sees war as avoidable by strength; inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: Favours tax cuts but relies on tariff and tax revenue; not a libertarian position.

harm-principle.rationale: No stated position; free speech and religious liberty planks coexist with moral regulation of drugs and gender.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individual rights such as guns and speech are stressed, but religious and national group claims also feature.

conscription.rationale: The platform raises troop pay and favours a modern professional force; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The platform stresses voting rights and election integrity; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Businessman-style governing and the Department of Government Efficiency.

positive-liberty.rationale: Merit-based, anti-entitlement framing and a limited-welfare orientation.

media-academia-power.rationale: Documented attacks on 'fake news' media and on universities and anti-intellectualism as components; the establishment-versus-people frame.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The official line is colorblind; hereditarian claims appear only on the fringe.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed; party-based electoral politics is assumed.

total-state.rationale: The stated aim is a smaller government and free speech; scholars note authoritarian tendencies but no totalising program.

national-rebirth.rationale: 'The golden age of America begins right now' after a period of decline.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The address says the Panama Canal is being taken back, and the administration has voiced annexation of Greenland and Canada.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Personalism is documented, but oath-based feudal authority is not a stated principle.

universal-morality.rationale: Religious conservative moral language is common; no explicit philosophical stance.

single-common-good.rationale: Populism's 'will of the people' resembles a single good, but no worked-out stance.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The platform says it will stand with Israel and the administration increased support.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened, and no clear adherent position; inferred neutral.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from pro-business orientation.

school-vouchers.rationale: The platform supports 'Universal School Choice in every State'.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The platform promises tax cuts and growth without balanced-budget rules; adherents are split.

economic-freedom.rationale: Pro-growth and deregulatory, but not articulated as a thesis.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rule is exercised through executive orders and enforcement; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: The 2017 address says every nation has the right to put its own interests first.

force-without-un.rationale: Strikes on alleged traffickers and Venezuela operation were carried out with no UN approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Evangelical support and appeals to faith; inferred.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The platform opposes extending benefits to illegal immigrants.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Implied by its emphasis on work and anti-dependency; not stated in the sources opened.

class-collaboration.rationale: Stresses national unity of all Americans over class divisions.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: National tradition is central and a revival of heritage a core appeal.

dominated-front.rationale: The administration pursues unilateral national interests, not a front with other states.

workers-nation.rationale: Appeals to American workers and 'Buy American, Hire American'.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Official policy is a two-sex binary, but no stated plank on distinct public roles for men and women.

ban-interest.rationale: The platform supports private finance and crypto; no such plank.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The inaugural address commits to a colorblind society and 'Equal Treatment for All' appears in the platform.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Populism blames an establishment, not a ruling class using the state; Marxist theory is rejected.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The address declares a national energy emergency and "drill, baby, drill", and the platform expands oil, gas and coal production.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The movement pairs national-culture preservation and a patriotic 'one nation' appeal with immigration restriction, implying newcomers should adopt American culture; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: Rhetoric about elites favouring open borders and a 'replacement' of voters circulates widely among adherents, though it is not in the platform; contested.

proportional-representation.rationale: The platform and movement defend existing winner-take-all and Electoral College arrangements; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: The 2017 address says America does not seek to impose its way of life, and the second administration disparages nation-building.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The 2025 address calls for a colorblind, merit-based society and two sexes, and the movement rejects claims of systemic sex bias.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The 2017 address says the establishment protected itself, not the citizens, and promises to return power to the people.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The platform's pro-life and family stance and its attachment to individual liberty from the state point against reproductive control; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The second administration sanctioned the ICC and opposes external courts judging American or allied forces, and the movement backs police and military.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The platform and administration use tariffs, state investment and entitlement protection, so the movement rejects a state limited to defence, courts and property.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Mainstream conservative and populist opinion treats marriage as a private choice; the movement does not call for discouraging interracial marriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The platform promises equal justice under the law for all Americans, though the movement also stresses citizens over non-citizens.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Inferred: the movement is anti-socialist and rejects the premise, which concerns Marxist theory it does not engage.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred: the movement celebrates American founding and westward settlement and rejects colonial guilt, though it has not addressed the question directly.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from the platform's emphasis on one national law for all citizens; the topic is not addressed directly.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The platform defends religious liberty and the freedom to practise and spread faith.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred: not part of the movement's agenda, and cattle farming is a strong part of its rural base.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The platform supports prayer and a greater role for faith in public life, and Christian-nationalist strands want religion in schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inferred: the movement opposes socialism and does not hold the Marxist doctrine of the state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Inferred: the inaugural address presents government as serving the people, but the movement's personalised executive pulls the other way.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred from the movement's hostility to the media, universities and the 'establishment' as biased, though it also claims facts of its own.

trade-surplus.rationale: Economic nationalism, tariffs and the view that trade deficits show other countries are taking advantage are central to the movement.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred: mass deportation targets illegal immigrants, not a minority as such, so a general power to expel hostile minorities is not stated.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The second administration's foreign policy uses force and threats for national interests, not only in response to aggression.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Inferred from the movement's emphasis on winning, strength and national rivalry.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Contested: rhetoric targets the 'radical left' and some call for bans, but the movement also presents itself as defending free speech.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Inferred: the movement stresses sovereignty and strong leadership rather than republican non-domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Split: the platform affirms the Constitution and federalism, but scholars note a personalised, strong executive.

vanguard-party.rationale: Inferred: a populist movement around a single leader rejects a revolutionary vanguard model.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Inferred: policy is framed as serving the 'forgotten' American citizen and worker, not ranking the poor first.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Home ownership is a platform theme and the movement favours private property over state provision; inferred, since council housing is not addressed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The platform backs right-to-work and a business-friendly labour stance, so limits on union action fit; inferred, as strikes are not discussed directly.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The movement blames elites, trade deals and open borders for hardship rather than population growth; inferred from the inaugural addresses.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The movement stresses a shared national culture and assimilation and treats mass immigration as a threat to unity; adherents are not uniform on it.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The movement is leader-centred and electoral and has no program of selecting officials by chance; inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The 2025 address declares a national emergency at the border and the movement favours broad executive powers against internal enemies; contested even among adherents.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The platform favours deregulation and lower prices through energy production and competition rather than ceilings; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: The 2025 address pledges to end government censorship and restore free speech, though the movement attacks the press as hostile.

party-commands-army.rationale: The platform places the military under the elected commander in chief and the state; no source supports party command. Inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The movement favours strict immigration controls and merit-based entry, so longer waits fit; the platform does not set a residence period. Inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not a theme of the platform or speeches; Trump gave away his salary but movement figures do not call for worker-level pay.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred from the movement's demand for loyalty to Trump and the platform line; adherents differ on how binding it should be.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The inaugural addresses are explicit about America First and national sovereignty over foreign institutions.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The movement favours a strong personalised executive and the unitary executive theory, which places command over the executive branch with the president.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Trumpism leans on evangelicals who organise by congregation or denomination; inferred, not stated.

clerical-rule.rationale: The platform backs religious liberty but within a constitutional republic; no plank gives clergy final political authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The addresses and platform rest on patriotism and national unity first, so working for one's own side's defeat is rejected.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The 2025 address stresses free speech, but the platform backs limits on material in schools; so censoring art is opposed in general.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Trump has mused about a third term while the platform is silent and the 22nd Amendment stands; adherents are split.

recall-officials.rationale: Not in the platform; populism favours more voter control but the movement has no stated recall plank.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: America First questions NATO-style burden sharing and troop commitments, but the platform keeps a strong military and alliances remain; the movement wants fewer commitments rather than none.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Property ownership and market housing are not threatened by the movement; banning rentals is inferred as far outside its free-enterprise stance.

people-in-arms.rationale: The platform calls for the strongest professional military and defends gun rights without proposing a citizen militia in its place.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The inaugural rhetoric appeals to the heartland and ordinary working people against urban elites; inferred, not stated as a moral claim.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The movement has made territorial statements about other countries but has no stated position on reunifying states divided by outside powers; inferred as indifferent.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Hostility to universities, experts and the establishment is a documented component of the movement.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Its patriotic rhetoric praises American and Western civilisation as superior; inferred from that rather than a stated rejection of equality of cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: The platform backs tough-on-crime policy and capital punishment for the worst crimes, and the administration has sought to expand its use.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The platform and the 2025 address oppose 'gender ideology' in schools and favour parental control of curricula, so the gender-equality part of this statement is resisted.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The platform stresses parental choice and 'patriotic' education, but creationism is not an official plank and adherents are split; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Social conservatives in the coalition favour restricting pornography, though the leader and libertarian-leaning supporters do not stress it; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The movement's immigration restriction includes moves to end birthright citizenship, which implies descent-based rules; inferred from that.

minority-language-support.rationale: Nationalist emphasis on a common national culture and English-language policy implies little support for minority-language provision; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The platform strongly defends religious liberty, though mainly for Christians; whether it extends to minority exemptions from general law is inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: A national-conservative stress on tradition and patriotic unity suggests little interest in promoting eccentricity; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred: America First emphasises national interest and deal-making; the movement has not backed debt cancellation for poor countries.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: the movement is capitalist and nationalist, favouring economic nationalism within the market system rather than transforming property relations.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred: the platform defends the existing Constitution and the movement is hostile to rewriting it.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The platform and inaugural address stress freedom and free speech, even though critics note illiberal tendencies; restriction for growth is not a stated position.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The America First approach prioritises American interests and the second administration cut foreign aid sharply.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The United States already has its own deterrent and the movement stresses military strength and sovereignty; read as keeping its own arsenal rather than relying on an ally.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Trump has criticised the Electoral College at times and defended it at others, and the platform is silent on abolishing it.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred: Trump has repeatedly pressed the Federal Reserve to cut rates and criticised its chair, which cuts against its independence.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The movement has backed Israeli territorial claims while also pursuing deal-based settlements, so adherents are not settled; the statement refers to a country's own homeland.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred: the platform defends private property and low taxes as rights, not as justified by their service to the common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The movement has no position on this scholarly debate about the Soviet Union.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from the platform's push to cut regulation and expand energy production.

collective-defense.rationale: Adherents are split between treating alliance duties as transactional and valuing them; the second administration's record is mixed.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred: the second administration pursued territorial claims such as Greenland and treated deals on territory as negotiable.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The platform defends religious liberty and the movement is hostile to curbing churches.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The movement presents the president as a partisan, personal leader of the nation's movement rather than a neutral figurehead.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from the movement's nationalism and stress on border and national integrity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred: the platform stresses one national system and hostility to foreign-style arrangements.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred: the movement is secular-populist or Christian-nationalist, not sacral kingship.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: the platform stresses tax cuts and exemptions rather than a flat rate.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred: the movement leans on conservative views of inherited traits and tradition.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Adherents claim presidential immunity while also saying no one is above the law.

space-expansion.rationale: The 2025 inaugural address promises to plant the American flag on Mars.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred: the movement reveres the Constitution but offers no view on mixed government.

leader-cult.rationale: Scholars describe a personalised movement around Trump, and rallies and merchandise celebrate him.

equal-parenting.rationale: Inferred: not addressed in the platform or addresses.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Socialism is rejected, so the claim is not engaged; the inaugural addresses stress national unity over class conflict. Inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: The platform defends private property and the movement is hostile to redistribution; taking estates is opposed.

refugee-return.rationale: The movement seeks to restrict refugee admissions and opposes mass return rights across borders; the question is not directly addressed, so inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The second administration voiced claims on Greenland and Panama on strategic grounds, not nationality; the nationality basis is rejected in favour of civic sovereignty, though it is inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The platform defends religious liberty as a constitutional freedom and American law protects leaving a faith.

women-must-cover.rationale: Legal dress mandates are alien to the platform, which stresses freedom and limited government; opposition is inferred.

common-currency.rationale: The movement stresses national sovereignty and distrusts supranational bodies; not directly addressed, so inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: America First nationalism favours separate sovereign states; the question is not addressed, so inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The platform stresses a common national culture and English-language assimilation; separate self-governing minority institutions are not on its agenda. Inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed directly; the colorblind-equality rhetoric suggests minorities should seek equal treatment at home. Inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The movement stresses national will, culture and leadership over economic determinism; inferred from its rhetoric.

ban-cartels.rationale: The platform stresses fighting big tech and drug-price collusion but opposes heavy regulation; adherents are split.

no-bailouts.rationale: Trump bailed out farmers and industries by tariff relief, while populists criticise bank bailouts; the movement is split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The movement attacks judges who block the elected president and the popular mandate, but it also invokes the Constitution; contested, inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The address and platform reject identity quotas in favour of merit-based, colorblind policy.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The movement wants tariffs and reshoring but not a closed bloc shutting off outside trade.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The platform opposes environmental regulation, though it favours protecting American workers through tariffs; binding standards are inferred to be rejected.

moral-incentives.rationale: The platform embraces markets and tax cuts as the spur to work and rejects collectivist ideals.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The movement works through elections and the existing constitutional order and opposes revolutionary insurrection.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inaugural rhetoric attacks elites and favours merit, but no hereditary titles exist; inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The movement stresses national pride and a patriotic telling of American history, as in the inaugural addresses.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: America First rejects nation-building and foreign tutelage; inferred from the foreign-policy stance, though territorial ambitions muddy it.

patriotic-education.rationale: The platform and inaugural addresses call for schools to teach patriotism and love of country.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The movement is committed to ending DEI and race-conscious preferences in admissions and hiring.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from its pro-market, anti-establishment stance; it distrusts the Federal Reserve but does not propose public money creation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Inferred from its pro-business, pro-growth economics; the movement does not expect capitalism to collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The United States has no predecessor empire in the relevant sense, and America First avoids imperial-style influence projects; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Trumpist economic nationalism uses tariffs to bargain for better terms, not to delink poor countries from the world market; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The movement courts rich-country workers as an exploited and neglected class, so it rejects this view; inferred from its populist appeal.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The platform backs religious liberty exemptions but does not defend a general right to discriminate; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The platform defends the Constitution and the First and Second Amendments as limits on government.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred: the movement stresses sovereignty and secure borders, with no claim that colonial borders be set aside.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred: the movement works within US elections and calls them the basis of the people's rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: a movement built on majority populism and a strong leader does not defend minority vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred: the movement presents itself as the people against a corrupt establishment that has broken faith.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred: scholars note a personalised executive, and Trumpists back presidential power over Congress and courts.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from the platform's conservative and rural base, though animal welfare is not a central theme.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from the platform's support for farming, hunting and agriculture.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Adherents are split between a religious-right duty tradition and an anti-elite populism that distrusts the wealthy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement is built on mobilising people to retake the country, as the inaugural address urges.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: Trumpists describe the media and universities as tools of an establishment that keeps people compliant.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: the inaugural address casts the establishment as ruling through institutions and the media against the people.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred: Trumpists attribute foreign gains to unfair trade at American expense, not poor countries being drained.

native-born-offices.rationale: Mixed: the movement is nativist on immigration but not documented as seeking to reserve offices by birth.

party-own-road.rationale: The movement is indifferent to the internal politics of communist and socialist parties abroad.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred: America First and the cuts to foreign aid favour independence over reliance on aid and loans.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred: its territorial statements concern future acquisition, not reopening past wars.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The 2025 inaugural address commits to a colorblind, merit-based society, which opposes ancestry-based leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred: Trumpists treat antifa as a threat and see anti-fascism as one partisan stance, not a founding value.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: the platform condemns communism, and the movement is hostile to both extremes of its opponents' labels.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Adherents are split; the movement makes no settled claim on the war's causes.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: the movement defends national heritage and resists removal of historic monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred: the 2025 address and the platform stress fairness for men and boys alongside a two-gender policy.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred: same grounds as for male disadvantage, with the platform's stress on equal protection.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: America First rejects exporting US institutions and the second administration's foreign policy declines democracy promotion.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred: the movement wants the military used for borders and order but under presidential command, not as a political guardian.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred: the platform's family policy treats care as a family matter and favours tax relief, not wages for housework.

filial-duty.rationale: The platform stresses the foundational role of families; filial duty is inferred from that social conservatism.

office-by-exam.rationale: The platform wants poorly performing employees fired and the state made accountable to elected leadership; exam-based selection is not stressed (inferred).

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The platform pledges to stop China buying American real estate and industries, in line with economic nationalism.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The platform praises the sanctity of marriage but is silent on divorce law; social conservatives are split (inferred).

recallable-delegates.rationale: The movement is built on a strong, personalised executive rather than delegate-style rule (inferred).

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The platform aims at long-term sustainability of Social Security, not its replacement with private accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Private property is central to the Republican platform and nothing suggests community land tenure (inferred).

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Platform stresses cutting spending but not Congress's purse power; Trump-era claims of executive spending discretion split adherents from congressional Republicans (inferred).

single-official-language.rationale: Nationalist cultural emphasis implies one national language; the platform is silent on it, so this is inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The platform opposes Chinese purchase of American real estate; a wider ban is inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The movement is hostile to DEI and group-based remedies, and would reject outcome-based findings of discrimination (inferred).

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Pro-business, consumer-economy populism; not a theme in sources (inferred).

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: America First stresses limited foreign commitments, and the platform says force is used sparingly where national interests are threatened.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: America First rejects costly interventions; the preamble says force is for clear national interests (inferred for bloc discipline).

corporate-influence.rationale: Anti-establishment rhetoric sits beside a business-friendly agenda, so adherents are split. Inferred from the movement's stated principles.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Hostility to NGOs, media and universities makes limits on foreign money congenial. Inferred from the movement's stated principles.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Pro-family and pro-birth appeals plus immigration restriction favour incentives over immigration. Inferred from the movement's stated principles.

residents-only-property.rationale: Concern about foreign land ownership exists, but local-residency limits cut against property rights and federal priorities. Inferred from the movement's stated principles.

job-guarantee.rationale: The platform pursues jobs through growth, tax cuts and tariffs rather than state employer-of-last-resort schemes. Inferred from the movement's stated principles.

democratic-peace.rationale: America First rejects nation-building and democracy promotion as foreign-policy aims. Inferred from the movement's stated principles.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The movement stresses law and order and respect for law enforcement. Inferred from the movement's stated principles.

non-intervention.rationale: Rhetorical restraint coexists with the second administration's use of force and pressure abroad, so the movement is split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union organisation is not a movement theme, and working-class appeals coexist with pro-business conservatism. Inferred from the movement's stated principles.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Mainstream adherents do not endorse conspiracy claims about a minority, though some fringe strands do. Inferred from the movement's stated principles.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Traditional family and marriage are part of the social-conservative component. Inferred from the movement's stated principles.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Calls for transparency coexist with hostility to the media and a personalised executive. Inferred from the movement's stated principles.

local-production.rationale: Buy American, tariffs and domestic manufacturing push toward producing and buying goods nearby, though mainly at national level.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement is centred on a strong personalised leader and the Republican party, not small informal groups. Inferred from the movement's stated principles.

national-law-over-international.rationale: America First sovereignty rhetoric puts national interest above international bodies and law.

religious-nation.rationale: The Christian-nationalist component wants a religious identity, but the platform frames religion as liberty, so adherents are split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: America First seeks leverage and concessions from other states but rejects subordinating the US to anyone; ritual tribute is not a stated aim, so the movement is left neutral.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: states' rights rhetoric favours local control, but the nation-first outlook opposes carving the country up; adherents are split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The platform defends private property and enterprise and rejects collective ownership of productive property.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from the movement's anti-communist and anti-socialist rhetoric and the platform's hostility to Marxism; Trump also negotiates with communist states, so it is not stronger.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The platform backs school choice and competition and choice in healthcare and veterans' care within publicly funded systems.

religion-illusion.rationale: The platform and inaugural addresses affirm religious faith and religious liberty as foundations of national life, the opposite of treating religion as a fading illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from the platform's pro-enterprise, pro-growth economics and nationalist praise of American industrial achievement; the movement offers no historical theory of capitalism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: the platform and addresses treat sex difference and the family as natural and ground equality in law, not in transforming the economy.

socialized-care.rationale: The platform and movement defend the traditional family and private care arrangements and oppose state-run domestic services.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from cultural nationalism and the 2025 English-language order, but no source calls for purging loanwords, so the answer is mild.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: the movement speaks of honouring tribal sovereignty rarely and is wary of binding commitments, but no source gives a settled view; adherents are split.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The movement is nationalist and market-oriented and rejects communal ownership as a model for society.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from nation-first nationalism; the platform does not promote settlement policy for the majority and the movement stresses individual and state-level control.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Trumpism is capitalist-leaning with economic-nationalist modifications and is hostile to communism; the 'third way' framing is not its own, so it mostly disagrees.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Adherents are split: biblical and historical ties are invoked in support of Israel, while the movement's own territorial talk rests on strategy and security rather than ancestry; nothing in the sources settles it.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial is not part of the platform or addresses; it appears only on the fringe, so a typical adherent rejects it, though the sources read never discuss the question.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Neither the platform nor the addresses call for criminalising same-sex relations, and the movement mainly contests marriage and gender policy rather than private conduct; inferred from that silence.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The inaugural address pledges to restore free speech, so adherents disavow suppression, though scholars cited on the movement note hostility to the media and illiberal tendencies.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The platform defends religious liberty within the constitutional order and proposes no blasphemy penalties; inferred from that framework.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: America First puts national interest first, but the sources never address colonial-style governance; territorial remarks about Greenland and Panama are strategic claims, so the answer is genuinely unclear.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: This is a doctrine of Islamic law that the movement does not hold and treats with suspicion, though it has no stated position on it; inferred from its security-first outlook.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The movement works through elections and constitutional law and does not endorse removing rulers by force over religious law; inferred from its program.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Trumpism claims to return power to the people against the establishment but is leader-centred and does not promote workplace or campus self-management, as scholars of its populism describe.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The address rejects race-based and identity-based social engineering in favour of a colourblind society, which is incompatible with an intersectional analysis.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The 2025 inaugural address states that policy will recognise only two sexes, male and female, which directly rejects legal recognition by gender identity.

assisted-dying.rationale: Neither source addresses it; the religious-conservative base opposes assisted dying, so the answer is inferred from the movement's pro-life and religious strands.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The movement defines itself against the left and the establishment while claiming to speak for ordinary people; some populists say they transcend left and right, but the sources do not support this.

alienated-labor.rationale: Trumpism speaks for workers hurt by globalisation but frames the problem as lost jobs, not alienation from creative activity; inferred from its economic nationalism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Trump's travel bans and rhetoric about radical Islamic terrorism suggest agreement, but the platform targets extremism and border security rather than Islam as such.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Religious rhetoric ('God's protection', Christian nationalist strands) is common, but the movement does not state that authority comes from God rather than the people.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from the platform's defence of religious liberty and Christian-conservative social stance; the movement has not addressed state dress rules.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's pro-business, anti-regulation stance and hostility to litigation, though the topic cuts across.

social-market-economy.rationale: The movement mixes tariffs, deregulation and defence of entitlements; it is neither laissez-faire nor a defined social market model.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The inaugural address and platform pledge to rebuild the military and make it the strongest ever.

rich-first.rationale: Trumpism prizes wealth and growth and promises prosperity for workers, but has no stated doctrine of letting some grow rich first; adherents are split.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: America First rhetoric favours staying out of foreign entanglements, though the US leads NATO and the second administration is interventionist; inferred and contested.

missingStatements.text: Millions of people living in the country illegally should be deported.
missingStatements.rationale: The platform pledges the largest deportation program in American history and the address vows to halt all illegal entry.

missingStatements.text: Government policy should recognise only two sexes, male and female.
missingStatements.rationale: The 2025 inaugural address makes this official policy; the answer to the existing statement is the reverse, agreeing with the same position.

missingStatements.text: Domestic oil, gas and coal production should be expanded.
missingStatements.rationale: The address declares an energy emergency and 'drill, baby, drill', and the platform expands oil, gas and coal production.

notes: Scholars disagree whether Trumpism is a coherent ideology; former adviser John Bolton says it lacks a philosophical core. Evangelical and Christian-nationalist strands, libertarian-leaning economic conservatives and nationalist-populist strands differ on abortion, welfare, same-sex marriage and the role of the state.
